Solution 3 is correct. The probability that Michael and James meet is 2/17.

**Recurrence.** Let P(n) be the probability that two specific players meet, with n players remaining (n ≡ 1 mod 3). In the first round:
- Both selected (probability 12/(n(n−1))): they meet.
- Exactly one selected and that player wins (probability 2(n−4)/(n(n−1))): both survive, so the chance of meeting later is P(n−3). If the selected player loses, they can never meet, so that case contributes nothing.
- Neither selected (probability (n−4)(n−5)/(n(n−1))): both survive, so P(n−3).

Combining the last two cases gives P(n) = 12/(n(n−1)) + (n−4)(n−3)/(n(n−1)) · P(n−3), with P(4) = 1.

**Closed form.** Check that P(n) = 4/n satisfies this. Substituting the hypothesis into the right side gives [12 + 4(n−4)]/(n(n−1)) = 4(n−1)/(n(n−1)) = 4/n. The base case P(4) = 1 holds, so by induction P(n) = 4/n, and P(34) = 4/34 = 2/17.
